chunks: And from him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Wasshash, from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abu Khadijah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"He (the father) and none of his dependents should eat from the 'Aqiqah (sacrificial meat)."
And he said: "For the midwife is one-third of the 'Aqiqah. If the midwife is the mother of the man or one of his dependents, she is not entitled to anything from it."
And she should make it into parts, then cook it, and distribute it, and give it only to the Ahl al-Wilayah (the Imams and their deputies/relatives).
And he said: "Everyone eats from the 'Aqiqah except the mother."

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْوِلَاةِ: Ahl al-Wilayah: The family of the Prophet/Imams or those entitled to their guardianship
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةِ: Aqiqah: Sacrificial animal slaughtered for a newborn child

ai.seo_question: What are the Shia jurisprudential rules for distributing 'Aqiqah meat and who is excluded from eating it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the jurisprudential distribution of the 'Aqiqah sacrifice, emphasizing the exclusion of the father and his dependents to distinguish the ritual offering from daily sustenance. It specifies that the midwife receives one-third unless she is a dependent, and mandates that the meat be distributed specifically to *Ahl al-Wilayah* (the Prophet’s family and their followers), with the mother explicitly excluded from consumption. This reflects the Shia emphasis on linking ritual acts to spiritual lineage and social hierarchy.
